The generated CUDA code will be compiled with nvcc on a Polaris A100 GPU (sm_80 architecture, 400 W TDP, 40 GB HBM2e, 6912 CUDA cores). PRIMARY GOAL — reduce GPU energy consumption (Joules) while preserving exact numerical correctness.  Energy = Power × Time; optimizations that reduce either average power draw OR execution time (or both) are valid. HARD CONSTRAINTS — correctness: (1) Preserve ALL program behavior, logic, and stdout output exactly. NEVER alter loop bounds, comparison operators, index arithmetic, or numerical computations — even if they appear to be off-by-one or redundant. (7) Do NOT change the program's command-line interface or output format. ENERGY OPTIMIZATION STRATEGIES: (A) Global memory coalescing: ensure threads in a warp access consecutive addresses. (B) Shared memory: cache frequently re-read global memory into __shared__. (C) Read-only cache: use __ldg() or const __restrict__ for read-only arrays. (D) Occupancy: tune thread block dimensions (multiples of 32, typically 128–256). (E) Warp divergence: use branchless arithmetic to reduce divergence. (F) Kernel fusion: merge consecutive kernels operating on the same data. (G) Arithmetic precision: replace double with float where acceptable; use fast-math intrinsics (__expf, __logf, __sinf). (H) Loop unrolling: add #pragma unroll for small inner loops. (I) Minimize synchronization: reduce __syncthreads() to only where strictly required. FORMAT: produce well-formatted C++ code with proper indentation and newlines. Every function body MUST span multiple lines — do NOT compact statements onto a single line.
